node_fixture.name: hashman_user_via_hashman
header: # Node fixture `hashman_user_via_hashman` for user_lock (harness title p8testuser) on the master-role node (kind
# puppetserver). It replaces the stand-in `hashman_lock_standin` (HQ after batch 20, item 6: the lift "the master-role
# node's hashman database"). user_lock locks a user that already exists in hashman's database; on a real master the
# user was created through hashman beforehand. Here hashman itself creates p8testuser, as an administrator would:
# `pp_auth.py useradd ... SILENT` (a new user starts locked, with an initial password hashman generates and prints),
# then `pp_auth.py unlock`, so that the lock user_lock applies is its own. No hash is seeded. The initial password is
# kept in /root/p8test-hashman-initial (0600) for the behaviour check that the locked user is refused although the
# password matches; it is a throwaway password of a p8test account on a lab node, never a real user's.
# Runs only if hashman's database has no entry for p8testuser yet, and before user_lock's exec.
# Lifted by: nothing needed — a test asset (rules/test_asset_fixtures.txt): the user is created by hashman itself.
node_fixture.scope_evidence: hashman_user_via_hashman (listed in rules/test_asset_fixtures.txt, a test asset, no mock-apply marker): file[/usr/local/sbin/p8test-create-hashman-user] is a root 0755 script that creates p8testuser through hashman's own 'pp_auth.py useradd ... SILENT', saves the throwaway initial password to /root/p8test-hashman-initial (0600, for the behaviour check) and 'pp_auth.py unlock's it; exec[p8test create p8testuser through hashman] runs it only when hashes.pp has no $p8testuser_pwd_hash entry (unless --check), requires hashman_base and is ordered before Exec['user_lock_p8testuser'] (a relationship only; no attribute of the class's exec is changed). Both resources only supply the pre-existing hashman user the define locks, within the stated asset scope; no seeded hash, no real account or NIC.
